title: Escrow release run blocking order confirmation

brief.headline: both guardians agree the decision belongs to a human
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 1449599 (settlement_worker/marketplace_escrow_release, idle in transaction, txn open 4.2s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 0% over 30s (120/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $18,400/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (settlement_worker/marketplace_escrow_release, pid 1449599) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $18,400/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Checkout at 0% success (120/120 failed over 30s) vs SLO 95%, $18,400/min at risk (BIZ-4). Blocker marketplace_escrow_release has ~896s expected remaining runtime, waiting costs ~$274,712 and EXCEEDS the 60s degradation tolerance (BIZ-5). However, blocker is PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT with never_interrupt policy and not replayable (BIZ-2), so I1 forbids termination. Waiting is also intolerable per I7. The Marketplace Payments owner must decide whether to interrupt the protected settlement ($12,500 in flight per DB-2) or accept continued checkout failure.

audit.report: The incident began when the escrow-release job marketplace_escrow_release entered a transaction that blocked order confirmation. Within 15 seconds checkout success fell to 55% (33/60) with 27 timeouts; after 30 seconds it was 0% (120/120 failed), putting $18,400/min at risk. The root blocker pid 1449599 held a transaction for 4.2s and was identified as a protected settlement job that is not replayable and has a never_interrupt policy. Both guardians determined that waiting or terminating was prohibited by policy, so they escalated the decision to Marketplace Payments. The final outcome was ESCALATED; no action was executed.
audit.root_cause: The escrow-release job marketplace_escrow_release (protected settlement, never_interrupt policy) entered a transaction that blocked checkout, and its policy prohibited any interruption, forcing escalation.
lessons: Add marketplace_escrow_release to the workload registry with its never_interrupt flag visible to all guardians before any action is taken.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian first proposed waiting then terminating, but the continuity guardian correctly blocked termination because the workload is PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT with never_interrupt, making termination prohibited regardless of cost; both guardians then agreed to escalate to a human.
follow_ups: Human decision-maker from Marketplace Payments reviews the workload registry entry and cost analysis to determine whether to modify the never_interrupt policy or create an interrupt-able variant.
After the human decision, update the change calendar and workload registry, and test a safe-to-interrupt path for future incidents.
